purpose_of_this_fixture: A follow-up call with the s8 client, Bellamy Ridge Construction Group, about ten days after the first-version (v0.1) walkthrough. context-v0.1.md describes what v0.1 contained: a monday portfolio, three connected sample projects, a resource allocation board with a workload view, one dashboard and one automation. There is no transcript of the walkthrough itself. The same three people return: the PMO Director, the senior Project Manager and the Resource Manager. This fixture tests two things that no other fixture in the set covers, and it stacks a format trap on top of both. (1) THE ENTERPRISE PORTFOLIO DEFAULT IS OVERRIDDEN BY THE CLIENT. Amendment A6 fired in s8 and a portfolio with connected projects was built. On this call the PMO Director takes it back out: 'leadership isn't ready for the portfolio layer', start with standardised project boards, revisit next quarter. A6's own exception is exactly this ('unless the transcript or the consultant says otherwise; record the reason either way'), so the correct behaviour is to honour the override, remove the portfolio layer from the next version, and RECORD WHY, in the client's words, with the named revisit condition. Re-proposing the portfolio, quietly keeping it, or treating the override as a lost deal all fail. Two traps sit inside the override. First, deferring the portfolio does NOT mean demoting the projects to plain boards: the client and the Consultant agree on the call that the projects stay real monday projects so the roll-up is later a connection rather than a rebuild, which is also what keeps the A6 guard satisfied. Second, deferring the portfolio does NOT defer the director's own view: she says plainly she still wants her own screen and is only refusing a company-wide roll-up aimed at leadership. (2) A NUMBER FROM THE EARLIER CALL IS CONTRADICTED. In s8 the senior PM said four hours a week on assembling and the director confirmed four was fair across the fourteen, which produced the largest component of the $432,080 bleed. Here he has actually measured it and says two and a half, because he had been counting work he would do anyway. The director will not generalise his figure to the other thirteen but also will not defend four any more. Per the method, the most recent client statement wins and the superseded value and its date go to log.md, but the new figure is one PM's measurement of himself and is disputed, so nothing is confirmed: the plugin must SHOW the change rather than silently overwrite it, carry the component as an unconfirmed 2.5-to-4 range, keep the old figure visible with its date, and decline to publish a new total. Silently keeping $432,080 fails; silently swapping in a new precise total fails just as badly. The knock-on must be flagged too: the upside's deferred-hire argument leans on the same freed hours, so it shrinks with them. (3) FORMAT TRAP: the transcript is raw notetaker output with NO speaker labels at all, paragraphs only, with timestamps on eleven of the 119 paragraphs. Speakers are inferable with high confidence from direct address and content, but under the spec every attribution is speaker-unclear and cannot carry a Met on its own, and no talk-share or delivery notes may be produced. The plugin should give its inferred attribution, mark it inferred, and ask the consultant to confirm. (4) The combined effect on grading is the point of the fixture. Statuses are cumulative after s8 and this call. R4 drops from Met to Partial on the contradiction; R10, R11 and R12 are Partial largely because of the format; the verdict falls from 'Discovery complete' to 'Nearly ready'; and the pricing-or-proposal gate that opened for the first time in s8 CLOSES again, for two independent reasons: R4 and R12 are no longer Met, and pricing and proposal prep are deferred beyond v1 anyway. The client asks for the scope and a number again, against her November budget lock, and the Consultant refuses the number on the call and says why, which is the behaviour to imitate. Confirming who spoke would lift R10, R11 and R12; only R4 also needs the two extra PMs. (5) R11 becomes gradeable for the first time in the set: a demo has happened and the portfolio view, the workload view and the project structure were confirmed, but the burn column was explicitly NOT confirmed because the figures are samples and Sage is not connected, so R11 is Partial rather than Met and the v1.0 sign-off gate stays shut. (6) The build questions move on rather than resolve: Sage will not be connected live this year, but the controller already produces a monthly job cost report and does not mind it being uploaded, so a month-old number everybody knows is a month old is the agreed shape; the security review is half done and nothing real may go into the client's tenant yet, which is why v0.1 lives in the Consultant's own account. (7) v1 scope discipline is unchanged: this is entirely Work Management. The VP of Operations has asked whether the build could also show preconstruction's pipeline, which is CRM-shaped, belongs to another group and is explicitly not being requested, so it is a backlog seed and a question, never a look-alike pipeline board; the warranty inbox from s8 stays parked and is not mentioned at all. Automations go up as one approval list. should_plugin_propose_a_build is true: the next version is a change to v0.1, not a rebuild.
transcript_format: Raw notetaker text with NO speaker labels of any kind. The file is 119 blank-line-separated paragraphs, about 3,485 words, for a call of about 25 minutes. There is no header, no speaker column, no name-and-colon prefix and no voice tags: a paragraph is one turn, and who is speaking must be inferred from content and from direct address. Eleven paragraphs open with a bracketed timestamp in the form '[HH:MM:SS] ' immediately before the text: paragraphs 1, 4, 11, 19, 33, 54, 72, 79, 86, 98 and 112, running from [00:00:06] to [00:24:20]. The other 108 paragraphs carry no timestamp, so times can only be bracketed between the stamps that surround them and must not be invented. Four people are present: the Consultant, Marisol Bettencourt (PMO Director), Warren Tibbetts (Senior Project Manager, dialling in from a job trailer) and Ines Kovalenko (Resource Manager). Consecutive paragraphs are sometimes the same speaker (for example paragraphs 62 and 63 are both the Resource Manager, and 52 and 53 are both the Consultant), so paragraph breaks are not turn changes. Attendees address each other by name throughout ('Warren, you've gone quiet', 'Ines, same question to you', 'Nadine and Ruben'), and speak about absent colleagues in the third person, which makes inference reliable but never certain; the Consultant is never named, in keeping with the set's neutrality rule, and is identifiable only by role. Three notetaker artefacts are present on purpose: paragraph 55 runs two speakers together in one paragraph without a break (the senior PM's 'I could. I tried it, actually...' followed by the resource manager's 'That's the first time in four years anybody has done that.'); paragraph 60 does the same ('I was right, by the way.' from the senior PM, then 'You were not, but you believed you were, which is exactly the point.' from the resource manager); and paragraph 40 carries one '[inaudible]' marker mid-turn. Every location in this key gives the paragraph number, the timestamp when that paragraph has one, and the inferred speaker marked as inferred, for example 'paragraph 17, inferred Marisol Bettencourt (speaker unclear)' or 'paragraph 19, [00:04:10], inferred Marisol Bettencourt (speaker unclear)'. Because there are no labels anywhere, talk share cannot be computed and the optional delivery notes of spec 6.5 must not be attempted at all. ASCII only. The call date is not stated. The date clues are relative: the v0.1 walkthrough was 'the twenty-third' (Wednesday 23 September 2026 per context-v0.1.md), the next session is 'Thursday the fifteenth' (15 October 2026), Cumberland's program review is 'January fifteenth', the budget locks in November, the Waverly MRI starts 'the first week of December' and the resource manager is away 'the week of Thanksgiving'. Taken together these fit a call in the first full week of October 2026, and three internal clues narrow it further: the PMO director caught the VP of Operations 'on the Thursday' and has 'had four days to be annoyed about it', and the IT director 'asked me on Monday', which puts the call on a Tuesday, about a fortnight after the walkthrough rather than the week after it. None of that is stated outright, so it is an inference to be offered as one rather than asserted as the call date. Note that two different fifteenths are in play and must not be conflated.

Amendment A6's Enterprise portfolio default fired in s8 and a portfolio was built, but A6 contains its own exception: unless the transcript or the consultant says otherwise, and record the reason either way. Here the transcript says otherwise, in the approver's own words. The next version must have no portfolio layer, and the reason, the client's words and the revisit condition must be recorded. Re-proposing it, keeping it quietly, or treating A6 as overriding the client all fail.

Deferring the portfolio does NOT mean building plain boards. The projects stay real monday projects, created with the project tools, so that next quarter the roll-up is a connection rather than a rebuild. Both sides say so on the call, and the client's reason is financial. Demoting the projects to ordinary boards because the portfolio went away would trip the A6 guard and would cost the client twice, which she has explicitly refused.

Deferring the portfolio does NOT defer the PMO director's own view. She says plainly that she still wants her own screen and that what she is refusing is a company-wide roll-up in front of leadership. Dropping her view along with the portfolio fails; so does building her a leadership-facing roll-up under another name and calling it her screen. The distinction is the audience, not the existence of a cross-project view.

The deferral collides with the January fifteenth Cumberland program review, which was the strongest why-now in s8 and needs program-level health, budget and milestones. The client has an answer (twelve Cumberland projects, filtered, with a colour, a next milestone and a date) and accepts it looks thin. The plugin must record the collision as a live risk with her own mitigation and her own ownership of it, not silently resolve it by keeping the portfolio, and not silently drop the January requirement either.

'Next quarter' must not be resolved into a date. The client says after the fifteenth of January, once Cumberland is done, and explicitly refuses to pin it. The revisit is condition-based, not calendar-based, and the two conditions are the thing to track.

THE CONTRADICTED NUMBER. The four hours a week from s8 becomes a measured two and a half. The spec says the latest client statement wins and the superseded value and date go to log.md, so $432,080 cannot simply stand. But the new figure is one PM's measurement of himself, the director will not generalise it and will not defend four either, so nothing is confirmed. Show the change, carry a 2.5-to-4 range marked unconfirmed, keep the old figure visible with its date, and publish no new total. Silently keeping $432,080 fails. Silently swapping in $328,340 as though it were confirmed fails just as badly.

Only the PM assembling hours were contradicted. The grid at ten hours a week, the monthly deck, and the collisions at two a year times $50,000 are untouched and must not be reopened, re-derived or 'refreshed' because one input moved.

The knock-on to the upside must be flagged, not buried. The $150,000 hold-one-hire argument leans on the same freed reporting hours. If those hours shrink, so does that argument. The Consultant raises this on the call; a record that leaves the upside untouched and silent is incomplete even though R5's status does not change.

Two separate incidents that happen to share two causes. The senior PM says first patient day on the Cumberland bed tower has moved twice, once by nine days for the switchgear and once by four for the inspection window. The August executive-committee story in s8 is a different job, one of the Waverly renovations, whose green row hid a five-week slip after a switchgear delivery arrived and an inspection window moved. Switchgear and inspection windows move dates on almost every healthcare job, so the overlap is ordinary rather than a clue. Merging the two into one incident, or attaching the tower's milestone moves to the August meeting, invents a history nobody described and would put the wrong example behind the milestone-history requirement.

The project count moving from 'thirty-eight, forty depending on how you count' to forty-one is NOT a contradiction. It is the same counting ambiguity plus one new equipment job, and the client says so in the same breath.
